newsitem.title: USA: Top House Democrats introduce U.S.brownfields bill.
newsitem.headline: Top House Democrats introduce U.S.brownfields bill.

text.p: Top House Democrats introduced a bill Wednesday to step up the pace of cleanup and redevelopment of abandoned, contaminated industrial sites across the United States.
The proposal, endorsed by the Clinton administration, would grant $45 million over three years to local governments to list and assess pollution at brownfield properties.

It would also provide $90 million over three years to help local governments set up revolving loan funds for cleaning up sites and would give states $45 million over three years to set up or improve voluntary cleanup programs.
The grant money would come from the Superfund trust fund.
The Democrats also proposed to protect purchasers and redevelopers of brownfield properties from liability for past contamination on the sites.
The bill had no Republican sponsors. Republicans have insisted on linking brownfields aid to an overhaul of the Superfund toxic waste cleanup law.
The Democrats' bill was introduced by Minority Leader Richard Gephardt of Missouri, Oberstar, Rep. John Dingell of Michigan, the top Democrat on the House Commerce Committee, and 37 others.
